in.mechanism: A falling baht makes Thai assets cheaper to foreigners but signals money leaving, and the leaving usually dominates.
Thailand imports nearly all of its energy. Expensive oil is a direct transfer out of Thai household spending and corporate margins.
Chinese demand and Chinese tourists are Thailand's largest single external input.
Thailand moves on foreign flows, and foreign flows move on how the world feels about risk — which is why Thai stocks fall on days when nothing happened in Thailand.

node.label: Thai equities
node.up: Thai equities are up — foreign money came back, or oil fell
node.what: The Stock Exchange of Thailand. Thailand imports its energy and exports tourism and goods, so it is hurt by expensive oil and helped by a weak dollar — and it moves on foreign flows far more than on anything domestic.
